title: Indian Market News Brief — 03 Nov 2026 — Nifty 50
quick_read: Strong earnings from market giant Reliance and falling crude oil prices helped Indian markets rise sharply. Proposals by the market regulator to cut taxes for foreign investors also boosted market mood. However, lower winter crop sowing and rising deposit interest costs for banks are key areas to watch.

stories.headline: Massive surge! Reliance Industries shares up 12% after Q2; add ₹2 lakh cr in mcap — when did RIL last rally this much?
stories.summary: Reliance Industries shares surged nearly 12% to ₹1,300 in a single day. The company reported record profit for the July-September quarter. The rally added ₹1.84 lakh crore to its total market value. This strong rise helped lift the main stock market indices by over 1.6%.
stories.impact: May help Nifty: Strong earnings from the heaviest weighted stock directly boost market index levels and investor confidence.

stories.headline: Sensex, Nifty tomorrow 3 Nov: Will stock market jump on Sebi's 12.5% foreign ‌investors LTCG tax removal recommendation?
stories.summary: Market regulator SEBI has recommended removing long-term capital gains tax for foreign investors. It also suggested tax relief for domestic mutual fund buyers. Market participants responded positively to reports of possible tax cuts. The government has not announced a final tax decision yet.
stories.impact: May help Nifty: Lower taxes for foreign investors could encourage higher foreign money inflows into Indian stock markets.

stories.headline: ITC shares to be in focus on Tuesday as Q2 net profit drops 18.5% on higher cigarette taxes
stories.summary: ITC reported an 18.5% fall in net profit to ₹4,229 crore for the September quarter. Higher taxes on cigarettes and costlier raw materials hurt profit margins. Operating profit from the cigarette business dropped over 27%. Overall company revenue still grew by nearly 44%.
stories.impact: May hurt Nifty: Reduced profit in a major index stock can drag down consumer sector share prices and overall index values.

stories.headline: Oil slide hands India's 10-year bond its best day since early April
stories.summary: Prices of Brent crude oil fell sharply in global markets. Lower oil prices reduce the total money India spends on imported fuel. Demand for Indian government 10-year bonds increased as oil prices dropped. The lower oil price trend helps lower domestic inflation pressure.
stories.impact: May help Nifty: Cheaper crude oil lowers input costs for Indian companies and reduces the national import bill.

stories.headline: A month after RBI’s rate hike, banks start raising deposit rates as liquidity shrinks, Bank of India the latest to move
stories.summary: Commercial banks in India have started increasing interest rates paid on customer deposits. Bank of India recently raised its deposit rates across several time periods. This step comes as spare cash available in the banking system has decreased. Banks are raising rates to attract funds for growing loan demand.
stories.impact: May hurt Nifty: Higher deposit rates increase interest expenses for banks, which could hurt their profit margins.

stories.headline: Sebi issues rules for depositary receipts on REITs, InvITs units
stories.summary: SEBI has introduced a new framework for depositary receipts on REITs and InvITs. This allows foreign investors to buy units of Indian real estate and infrastructure trusts on foreign exchanges. Fresh offerings require approval from exchanges and 75% consent from unitholders. The move aims to attract foreign capital to Indian infrastructure.

stories.headline: India’s rabi acreage down 46% as sowing of all crops gets delayed
stories.summary: Planting for winter crops in India has dropped 46% compared to normal levels. Sowing of mustard fell 47%, while pulse crops dropped 52%. Wheat and rice planted areas are also lower than last year. Delays in sowing raise concerns over future food supply and rural income.
stories.impact: May hurt Nifty: Lower crop output could drive up food prices and reduce consumer spending power in rural areas.

stories.headline: Small-cap sell off intensifies as MTF funded positions unwind
stories.summary: Money borrowed by stock traders for margin trading fell to ₹1.51 lakh crore in October. Traders reduced their debt-funded positions due to weak quarterly company profits and higher interest rates. This reduction in leverage led to selling pressure in smaller company shares.
stories.impact: May hurt Nifty: Less borrowing by traders reduces general buying activity and puts downward pressure on stock prices.
